title: Literature check: neural-field comets are a variant of depression-driven traveling spots (Bressloff-Kilpatrick 2011); Particle Lenia ring fission has no precedent; slow-exterior walls match the diffusion-limited (Mullins-Sekerka) division mechanism
summary: Prior art for the results since c00's 16:53 sweep. c20's neural comets are a variant: traveling spots from synaptic depression and bump splitting are published, a steady multiplying spot gas is not. The E fork cuts the factor that scales all coupling, which is closer to switching connectivity off than to starving a body. c18's food-eating Flow-Lenia dividers vary Plantec et al. 2025, which has food but no division or fed/starved test. c13's Particle Lenia ring fission has no precedent in the original article. The slow-exterior wall results fit Zwicker's diffusion-limited division. New operator: feedback-stabilised excitable fragments (Zykov-Showalter), whose size is unstable without feedback, as a route to motile repair.

prior_art.nearest: Bressloff & Kilpatrick, SIAM J Appl Math 71:379 (2011); Owen, Laing & Coombes, NJP 9:378 (2007)
prior_art.note: A traveling spot from depression and bump splitting are published. A steady 2D gas of 30-40 multiplying spots with tracked lineages is not.

prior_art.nearest: Reynolds, Ponce-Dawson & Pearson, PRE 56:185 (1997) (UNVERIFIED); Tsodyks-Markram depression as in Bressloff & Kilpatrick 2011
prior_art.note: The fork removes r, which multiplies all coupling, so it switches connectivity off. A graded cut that shows individual starvation would make E stronger.
Food to matter with decay is published. Division, lineages and the starved-daughter fork are new.
The original article reports no rings or fission.

prior_art.nearest: Zwicker et al., Nat Phys 13:408 (2017), diffusion-limited shape instability
prior_art.note: A slow exterior sharpens the edge supply gradient that drives Mullins-Sekerka-type splitting, whatever the cause of the slowness.
